office_does: Klickitat County's three commissioners adopt the county budget and ordinances, set land-use policy and oversee county departments, including the county jail; each is nominated by district and elected by the whole county.
race_blurb: First-term Commissioner Lori Zoller, who led the August primary 1,148 to 760, faces State Parks ranger Andy Kallinen of Lyle; both prefer the Republican Party. Kallinen faults how the county took over the jail and wants more deputies, dispatchers and a crisis responder; Zoller runs on a leaner reorganization, a stable budget and writing a data-center ordinance instead of a moratorium.

candidates.summary: First-term District 2 commissioner with three decades of county project work (rails-to-trails, watershed and salmon recovery) and chair of regional aging, housing, airport and health boards.
highlights: Says a reorganization done in-house 'made us leaner,' cutting costs through attrition with no layoffs [S2]
Defends the county's takeover of jail operations and credits her term with bringing the jail into compliance [S1][S2]
Opposed a six-month data-center moratorium in favour of writing an ordinance; sees data centers as possible tax base [S2][S3]
Wants to diversify county revenue beyond the Roosevelt landfill and explore managing state timber trust lands locally [S2]
Led the August primary with 1,148 votes [S6]

experience.basis: Sitting commissioner running on her first-term record, with about 30 years of county project work and chairs of several regional boards; only one term in this office.

spending.basis: Credits leaner reorganization by not backfilling positions and a hiring freeze, while also seeking new revenue and grants rather than cuts alone.

candidates.summary: Washington State Parks ranger and assistant area manager with 30-plus years in law enforcement and 20 years in the Army National Guard and Coast Guard Reserve; ran for LD 14 in 2024.
highlights: Platform of 'Responsible, Effective, Accountable, Limited' county government [S2]
Wants at least two more deputies, more 911 dispatchers and a dedicated mental-health crisis responder [S2][S3]
Says the way the jail transition was handled 'was terrible,' though he does not oppose a separate corrections department [S3]
Wants the county fairly compensated for hosting energy projects and to plan for data-center power demand [S2][S3]
Finished second in the primary with 760 votes [S5]

experience.basis: Has never held county office and is challenging the incumbent, though he brings decades of state service, a union executive-board seat and a community council seat.

safety.basis: Calls public safety government's first job and wants more deputies and dispatchers, but also a dedicated crisis responder and says jail should be the last resort for people in mental-health crisis.

spending.basis: Runs on 'Limited' government and protecting existing revenue while proposing added deputies, dispatchers and a crisis responder.

reform.basis: Criticizes current leadership's process as 'winging it' and says 'You can't just do business as usual,' proposing a methodical root-cause approach and new recruitment strategies.
